author: user
text: One reconnect in forty is worse than it sounds — a session of any length hits it more often than not. What makes you confident this belongs in the first patch rather than holding the ship?

author: claude
text: Two things. Nothing is lost either way — the edits stay queued, so the worst of it is a reader watching a spinner until they background the app. And the workaround is written and tested: resending on a twenty-second timer turns the stall into a delay nobody watches. What would actually remove it is the vendor fix, and they have acknowledged it without naming a date, so holding the ship means holding it on someone else's release. If you read that trade differently, choose Request another pass below and I will plan around it.

author: user
text: Fine for the first patch — I would take the feature over holding it for someone else's release. What I don't want is this sitting open in a month because the day it shipped it stopped being anyone's problem. What happens if their release comes and goes without the fix in it?

author: claude
text: Then the workaround is what ships, and it keeps working: a delay stays a delay whether they fix it or not. What I don't want is for that to become the answer by inaction, which is the shape you're describing. Tick what I should carry into the patch and press Done when the list is right — none of it starts before the ship.
markup:
If their release comes and goes, what should I have ready?

Go back to them monthly until there is a date or a no Clear the stall ourselves, so nobody has to background the app Say what the spinner is, where the reader is looking at it

author: claude
text: The vendor release is the only schedule we do not control. Should this task stay blocked until their fix is in our build, even if the workaround ships first?

author: user
text: Does the support playbook cover the background-app case, or only the spinner?

author: claude
text: Both — it opens on the spinner and ends with the background-app recovery, which is the step support was missing.
